sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. November 13, 2025 announcement explicitly releases gpt-5.1-codex and gpt-5.1-codex-mini as coding-agent models. Neither a nominal total nor an active parameter count is stated; the general GPT-5.1 benchmark table reports capability scores, not Codex size.

sources.title: Codex changelog: Introducing GPT-5.1-Codex and GPT-5.1-Codex-Mini
sources.evidence: Direct HTML fetched after the web reader hit its size limit. November 13, 2025 entry explicitly introduces both model options alongside the API launch and makes gpt-5.1-codex the CLI/IDE default on macOS and Linux that day. No earlier original 5.1-Codex release was found in this changelog.

sources.title: GPT-5.1-Codex API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh original Markdown fetched HTTP 200 on October 27, 2026 and exact model documentation retrieved again through OpenAI Docs. Confirms 400,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens, function calling, image input, prompt caching and Responses-only support. The alias is regularly updated; its only listed snapshot is the undated alias and the Markdown status is shut down. The heading identifies a GPT-5.1 coding version but provides no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Directly fetched archived guide expressly covers models before GPT-5.6. It explains prompt caching through Transformer attention key/value projections, with KV tensors cached across layers and heads. This mechanism plus exact model caching support permits only a broad operational Transformer inference.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly fetched guide explains that Responses input_file PDFs are converted to extracted text and page images for vision-capable models. This is an API file-format convention, not an extra native neural modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Directly fetched April 22, 2026 legacy notice explicitly lists gpt-5.1-codex among models whose API access shut down on July 23, 2026. This is consistent with its current model-page status.

sources.title: Building more with GPT-5.1-Codex-Max
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The November 19, 2025 successor announcement and exact GPT-5.1-Codex comparison column report reasoning-token efficiency and SWE-bench/SWE-Lancer/Terminal-Bench results, with no size or activated-parameter column. Max is built on an update to the foundational reasoning model; its training and compaction details are not original Codex parameter specifications.

sources.title: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full 27-page original PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27, 2026; complete text searched for parameter counts and relevant passages reread. Table 6 compares original gpt-5.1-codex destructive-action avoidance with Max and GPT-5-Codex. The introduction describes Max as built on an updated foundational model. Neither nominal total nor active parameters are supplied for original 5.1-Codex; benchmark percentages and Max-specific training do not establish its size.

sources.title: A Practical Approach to Verifying Code at Scale
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. December 1, 2025 Codex-team research labels GPT-5.1-Codex in precision/recall and inference-budget figures. It expressly identifies code generation and review as different tasks of the same underlying model, but gives no nominal total, active parameter count or routing inventory. Its budget is token spend, not activated parameters.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves service intellectual-property rights and grants limited use rights. Used as a descriptive proprietary service classification, not as a named open-weight license or exact November 2025 contract wording.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Directly fetched catalog lists GPT-5.1-Codex as a retired hosted model, separately from the explicit Apache-2.0 open-weight gpt-oss section.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh original Markdown fetched HTTP 200 October 27, 2026 and read in full for the explicitly named GPT-5.1 lineage. It lists the gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 snapshot, context/output limits and API features, but no nominal total or active parameter count. A named-base relationship therefore supplies no numerical size to inherit.

sources.title: BioTool: A Comprehensive Tool-Calling Dataset for Enhancing Biomedical Capabilities of Large Language Models
sources.publisher: Xin Gao et al., UC San Diego and MBZUAI
sources.evidence: Original May 2026 research-team paper reopened and complete HTML fetched HTTP 200 October 27, 2026. Tables 1, 2, 3 and 5 label GPT-5.1-Codex but report task scores, API success and argument-error rates, with no total or active parameter column. The introduction vaguely describes commercial models as having hundreds of times more parameters; this is not a model-specific nominal size or reliable bound. Its Codex reference points to the Max system card, further limiting identity precision. No count is adopted.

sources.title: SWE-Refactor: A Repository-Level Benchmark for Real-World LLM-Based Code Refactoring
sources.publisher: Yisen Xu, Jinqiu Yang and Tse-Hsun Chen, Concordia University
sources.evidence: Original February 2026 paper reopened and complete HTML fetched HTTP 200 October 27, 2026. Section 4.4 explicitly tests GPT-5.1-Codex, giving 151/200 successful refactorings and atomic/compound performance. These are task counts and success rates; no nominal total or active model-parameter count is reported. Original OpenReview endpoints encountered a browser challenge, so the read source is this accessible author paper on arXiv.

sources.title: Foundry Models sold by Azure: GPT-5.1 capabilities
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Provider specification table identifies gpt-5.1-codex (2025-11-13) separately from mini and Max. Its columns cover capabilities, context, output and training-data cutoff; none supplies total or active parameter counts.

name.note: Official exact model name; adds the published hyphen before Codex.

developer.note: First-party release announcement identifies OpenAI as the developer.

family.note: Original 5.1-Codex is a specialized GPT-5.1 variant, distinct from 5.1-Codex-Max, mini and original GPT-5-Codex. Replaces cross-generation gpt-codex grouping.

release_date.note: Original dated API release and Codex CLI/IDE availability both establish November 13, 2025. Not the November 12 ChatGPT GPT-5.1 release or later Max launch.

open_weights.note: Reviewed first-party distribution is hosted Codex/API access under reserved service rights; the catalog separately identifies downloadable open-weight models.

license.note: Descriptive classification of this hosted model, rather than an SPDX or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: October 27 re-audit found no published nominal total in the exact model documentation, launch, later OpenAI comparisons/training research, provider table or original BioTool/SWE-Refactor research. GPT-5.1 is explicitly named as the coding variant's base, but its own documentation supplies no count to inherit. BioTool's vague size comparison and inconsistent Max citation establish neither a model-specific size nor a bound. Fresh exact-model total/size/billion searches found no qualifying specification; no black-box estimate or sibling count is adopted.

active_parameters_b.note: Independently rechecked active and activated parameters on October 27, including targeted searches and later original research-team comparison tables. OpenAI publishes token-efficiency and inference-budget results; BioTool and SWE-Refactor publish performance/argument metrics, with no activated-parameter convention for this exact model. Neither nominal active size nor routing is established. No dense-equals-total inference, Max/mini transfer or black-box estimate is used.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source operational inference: exact model documentation explicitly supports prompt_caching and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 guide explains its Transformer attention KV mechanism. This does not establish an exclusively Transformer block inventory, layer/head dimensions, dense/MoE routing or counts; training research does not disclose those details.

context_window.note: Exact documented context window, distinct from the 128,000 maximum output. No maximum input is stated on this page; none is derived by subtraction. Limits are documentation evidence, not an endpoint test.

modalities.note: Native input is text/image and output is text. PDF denotes supported Responses API processing into text/page images for this vision-capable model; absence of a file_uploads flag is not a documented denial. No audio/video or image output is inferred.

reasoning.note: Exact model page explicitly supports reasoning tokens; later comparison evaluates original 5.1-Codex at high reasoning effort. General GPT-5.1 none-mode defaults are not transferred.

tool_call.note: Exact model page explicitly supports function calling in the Responses API.

description.value: GPT-5.1 variant for coding agents, with text and image input, reasoning, function calling and a 400,000-token context window.
description.note: Replaces generic product positioning with documented specialization and capabilities.

patch.notes: Original GPT-5.1-Codex became available in Codex and the API on November 13, 2025. It is distinct from GPT-5.1-Codex-Max and mini. The API documentation describes a mutable alias and supplies no dated immutable snapshot. The documented context is 400,000 tokens, with a separate 128,000 maximum output; no maximum input is supplied. PDF input denotes API conversion into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified operational inference from exact prompt-caching support and the applicable Transformer KV-cache explanation; complete block design and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. Nominal total and active parameters remain undisclosed; the named GPT-5.1 base also has no published count to inherit. API access shut down on July 23, 2026; specifications are last-documented capabilities, not a claim of current endpoint operation.

summary: Preserved the twelve non-parameter assessments. Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit reopened exact GPT-5.1-Codex and named-base documentation, launch sources, Max comparisons/system card, code-review training research and the Azure specification table. Separately searched total and active counts and inspected later original BioTool and SWE-Refactor research: no qualifying nominal size or activated-parameter convention was found. Both counts remain explicitly null/undisclosed; rejected vague commercial-model size comparisons and cross-model transfers.
